simple.meaning: קוּץ (qûwts) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to be (causatively, make ) disgusted or anxious.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 9 times across Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, 1 Kings, and 2 more, beginning at Genesis 27:46. Its contexts include family line, land, wilderness, Egypt, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to קוּץ (H6973).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: קוּץ (qûwts) / H6973 is traced through Genesis 27:46, Exodus 1:12, Leviticus 20:23, Numbers 21:5 as a generated source-based concept entry.

occurrences.englishText: Rebekah said to Isaac, “I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth. If Jacob takes a wife of the daughters of Heth, such as these, of the daughters of the land, what good will my life do me?”
But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and the more they spread out. They started to dread the children of Israel.
You shall not walk in the customs of the nation which I am casting out before you; for they did all these things, and therefore I abhorred them.

The people spoke against God and against Moses: “Why have you brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? For there is no bread, there is no water, and our soul loathes this disgusting food!”
Moab was very afraid of the people, because they were many. Moab was distressed because of the children of Israel.
He was an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon, in addition to the mischief of Hadad. He abhorred Israel, and reigned over Syria.
My son, don’t despise Yahweh’s discipline,
“Let’s go up against Judah, and tear it apart, and let’s divide it among ourselves, and set up a king within it, even the son of Tabeel.”
For before the child knows to refuse the evil and choose the good, the land whose two kings you abhor shall be forsaken.
